		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[LIKES_SITE:DARK_FORTRESS]
	[LIKES_SITE:CAVE]
	[LIKES_SITE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CAVE]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:DARK_FORTRESS]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:TREE_CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]

	[START_BIOME:ANY_TROPICAL_RIVER]
	[START_BIOME:ANY_TROPICAL_WETLAND]
	[START_BIOME:ANY_TEMPERATE_WETLAND]
	HA fix: broaden starting placement so the civ reliably generates (CKC's
	wetland-only START_BIOME left worlds with few such biomes kobold-less).
	MOUNTAIN + NOT_FREEZING match vanilla kobold breadth; the tropical/wetland
	START_BIOMEs above and BIOME_SUPPORT weights below keep their swamp-cave lean.
	[START_BIOME:MOUNTAIN]
	[START_BIOME:NOT_FREEZING]

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE_DETAILED]

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE_DETAILED]

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[LIKES_SITE:DARK_FORTRESS]

	[LIKES_SITE:CAVE_DETAILED]

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

	Dread Wyrm -- the ancient-dragon king. ALLOWED_CLASS gates the throne to the Ancient Dragon caste
	(CREATURE_CLASS HA_DRAGON_RULER); with no living dragon in the civ the throne simply sits vacant.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[LIKES_SITE:DARK_FORTRESS]

	[LIKES_SITE:CAVE_DETAILED]

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[LIKES_SITE:DARK_FORTRESS]
	[LIKES_SITE:CAVE]
	[LIKES_SITE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CAVE]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CAVE_DETAILED]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:DARK_FORTRESS]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:TREE_CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]

	[START_BIOME:ANY_TROPICAL_WETLAND]
	[START_BIOME:ANY_TEMPERATE_WETLAND]
	HA fix: broaden starting placement so the civ reliably generates (CKC's
	wetland-only START_BIOME left worlds with few such biomes kobold-less).
	MOUNTAIN + NOT_FREEZING match vanilla kobold breadth; the tropical/wetland
	START_BIOMEs above and BIOME_SUPPORT weights below keep their swamp-cave lean.

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CAVE
		LIKES_SITE:CAVE
		DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:PLAYER_FORTRESS
		LIKES_SITE:PLAYER_FORTRESS

	Added broad tolerance for moving into other sites. Kobolds aren't picky.

	HA fix history: CAVE_DETAILED (v<=0.10, = MountainHalls) needed mountain
	starts and lost the niche to dwarves -> 0 civs. CAVE (v0.11) ALSO placed 0
	civs: Cave sites are pregenerated terrain features that only SKULKING civs
	move into -- a non-SKULKING civ must FOUND its default site at worldgen, and
	Cave is not foundable (verified live: HA_KOBOLD_CAVES 0 civs vs vanilla
	SKULKING 3 in the same world, with near-identical baked start biomes).
	v0.12: DARK_FORTRESS ("pits") -- foundable by any civ regardless of biome
	(verified in the same world: HA_ILLITHID_CIV founded 3 DarkFortress civs)
	and it fits the warren/pit-boss flavor. CAVE stays liked/tolerated so
	kobolds still move into caves after worldgen.

	Vanilla kobold ethics are fairly egalitarian, without heirarchy, central government, or capital punishment. Positions have been designed to reflect decentralized local-level leadership. As population grows, major positions are replaced with more prestigious mini-nobles, elected by general consensus, who become increasingly demanding of trinkets and nicer conditions.

	generated mythical entity pairs it with SITE_GUARDIAN and the DIVINE_MAT tokens
	and has zero population. Putting it on a farming civ made worldgen reject every
	world with FARMING CIVILIZATION PLACED WITHOUT CROPS.

	generated mythical entity pairs it with SITE_GUARDIAN and the DIVINE_MAT tokens
	and has zero population. Putting it on a farming civ made worldgen reject every
	world with FARMING CIVILIZATION PLACED WITHOUT CROPS.

	No LAYER_LINKED. It was tried and reverted: a layer-linked civ behaves like the
	vanilla animal peoples, which hold 230 civilizations and zero sites. Drow fell to
	3 entities and no sites at all, illithids vanished from the world outright, so
	neither could be embarked as.
	No MYTHICAL here. That flag belongs to angel/vault style entities: DF's own
	generated mythical entity pairs it with SITE_GUARDIAN and the DIVINE_MAT tokens
	and has zero population. Putting it on a farming civ made worldgen reject every
	world with FARMING CIVILIZATION PLACED WITHOUT CROPS.

	vanilla animal peoples, which hold 230 civilizations and zero sites. Drow fell to

	neither could be embarked as.

	generated mythical entity pairs it with SITE_GUARDIAN and the DIVINE_MAT tokens
	and has zero population. Putting it on a farming civ made worldgen reject every
	world with FARMING CIVILIZATION PLACED WITHOUT CROPS.

	generated mythical entity pairs it with SITE_GUARDIAN and the DIVINE_MAT tokens

	world with FARMING CIVILIZATION PLACED WITHOUT CROPS.

	vanilla animal peoples, which hold 230 civilizations and zero sites. Drow fell to
	3 entities and no sites at all, illithids vanished from the world outright, so
	neither could be embarked as.

	generated mythical entity pairs it with SITE_GUARDIAN and the DIVINE_MAT tokens
	and has zero population. Putting it on a farming civ made worldgen reject every
	world with FARMING CIVILIZATION PLACED WITHOUT CROPS.

	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---

	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.

	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]

	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.

	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]

	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	--- sites: a few human-style castles, little expansion ---
	BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS turns mead halls into castles, but only at hamlet or
	town sites, which is why it does nothing for the succubi: they carry the token and
	land holders both, and build CAVE_DETAILED. High elves build towns, so it should
	apply here. The other half of the requirement, a LAND_HOLDER position, is on the
	Lady of Light below.
	[BUILDS_OUTDOOR_FORTIFICATIONS]
	[DEFAULT_SITE_TYPE:CITY]
	[LIKES_SITE:CITY]
	[TOLERATES_SITE:CITY]
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with no SETTLEMENT_BIOME and no START_BIOME. Per the raw
	reference that founds one settlement and no more. Territory spread is NOT the
	limiter: BIOME_SUPPORT numbers are relative to each other only, so a lone entry at
	weight 1 still puts the entire expansion budget into forest. What actually grants
	the right to build is SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME, so those are gone.
	BIOME_SUPPORT has to stay: with none at all worldgen rejects every candidate world.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_FOREST]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_FOREST:1]

	human civilization fighting humans for the same tiles, and winning: 547 sites against
	533, on hills 293 against 264 and grassland 214 against 207. They are pushed onto the
	harsh margins instead. Prime grassland is left to the humans at weight 1, and the
	ANY_OCEAN:12 that let them island-hop the whole coastline is cut to 1.

	took the badlands nobody else wanted, 148 desert sites, and finished ahead of the
	humans again on both population and site count. With desert gone their territory
	cannot spread through it either, so they cannot conquer across it.

	Mountain-tribe pattern, matching the drow, succubi and dark dwarves: start in the
	mountains, settle mountain/forest/grassland/savanna/shrubland, and support the
	subterranean layers. The earlier no-territory-in-the-start-biome experiment held them
	to 31 entities and a death spiral, so it is retired.
	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region
	type derived from elevation, and a hill region is classified underneath whichever of
	the open biomes covers it. So the closest expressible form of mountains-and-hills is
	MOUNTAIN plus the open classes, with forest dropped.

	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region
	type derived from elevation, and a hill region is classified underneath whichever of
	the open biomes covers it. So the closest expressible form of mountains-and-hills is
	MOUNTAIN plus the open classes, with forest dropped.

	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region

	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region
	type derived from elevation, and a hill region is classified underneath whichever of
	the open biomes covers it. So the closest expressible form of mountains-and-hills is
	MOUNTAIN plus the open classes, with forest dropped.

	Mountain-tribe pattern, matching the drow, succubi and dark dwarves: start in the
	mountains, settle mountain/forest/grassland/savanna/shrubland, and support the
	subterranean layers. The earlier no-territory-in-the-start-biome experiment held them
	to 31 entities and a death spiral, so it is retired.
	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region
	type derived from elevation, and a hill region is classified underneath whichever of
	the open biomes covers it. So the closest expressible form of mountains-and-hills is
	MOUNTAIN plus the open classes, with forest dropped.

	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region

	Mountain-tribe pattern, matching the drow, succubi and dark dwarves: start in the
	mountains, settle mountain/forest/grassland/savanna/shrubland, and support the
	subterranean layers. The earlier no-territory-in-the-start-biome experiment held them
	to 31 entities and a death spiral, so it is retired.
	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region
	type derived from elevation, and a hill region is classified underneath whichever of
	the open biomes covers it. So the closest expressible form of mountains-and-hills is

	Mountain-tribe pattern, matching the drow, succubi and dark dwarves: start in the
	mountains, settle mountain/forest/grassland/savanna/shrubland, and support the
	subterranean layers. The earlier no-territory-in-the-start-biome experiment held them
	to 31 entities and a death spiral, so it is retired.
	Mountains and hill country. There is no HILLS biome token in DF: hills are a region
	type derived from elevation, and a hill region is classified underneath whichever of
	the open biomes covers it. So the closest expressible form of mountains-and-hills is
	MOUNTAIN plus the open classes, with forest dropped.

	there is no ALL wildcard. Passing ALL leaves BOTH lists empty and the entity
	fails finalization ("Gem shape not found: ALL"), which is why this must stay a
	written-out list like every other entity in the suite.

	and GEM_PREF; WOOD_PREF, METALWORKING, MELEE_EQUIPMENT, RANGED_EQUIPMENT,
	SIEGE_ENGINEER, SOAP_MAKER and GENERATED were all rejected as unrecognised

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]

	No LAYER_LINKED: ha-illithids proved a layer-linked civ ends up with hundreds of
	civilizations and zero sites, so it cannot be embarked as.

	Placement and expansion, following the pattern ha-forest-golems and ha-high-elves already
	use: EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME with NO SETTLEMENT_BIOME and NO START_BIOME. That combination
	founds one settlement and no more, because SETTLEMENT_BIOME and START_BIOME are what grant
	a civ the right to build, and neither is here. There is no token that says "do not expand";
	withholding the right to build is the mechanism.

	BIOME_SUPPORT is NOT the limiter -- its numbers are relative to each other only -- but it
	cannot be dropped either: with no BIOME_SUPPORT at all worldgen rejects every candidate
	world. The three weights below are the human ones for the biomes humans start in.

	Where humans go: vanilla PLAINS starts in ANY_GRASSLAND, ANY_SAVANNA and ANY_SHRUBLAND.
	EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME takes a single biome everywhere it is used (vanilla uses it once, for
	dwarves; both HA mods above use one), so warlocks start in the grassland and the other two
	appear only as support. Whether several EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME entries are legal is untested.
	[EXCLUSIVE_START_BIOME:ANY_GRASSLAND]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_GRASSLAND:3]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SAVANNA:2]
	[BIOME_SUPPORT:ANY_SHRUBLAND:2]
